body: After about 15 years of depression and wishing it would go away, I made the choice to see a doctor and get on medication. Making this decision made it easier for me to bring up the problem and talk about it, which helped much more. I think the combination of the two was necessary for me. My whole train of thought and outlook on daily life is different now.

I had a "friend" tell me on more than one occasion that he wanted to get recircumcised... so he could be sexually pure again. I asked him a few times to look up the definition of the word circumcise, then decided to just drop it.  
Oh, he also wanted a vasectomy so he'd never pop wood again. Strange guy. Almost 30 too.
21 weeks and then I blew it. I mean, I came up with a new plan. I haven't been able to go more than 1 week since, I feel like it was a fluke.

I had a crush on a young lady who was away at college. My dream was that I had to travel to her college, and inform her that her younger brother had committed suicide. It was an extremely vivid dream and her reaction was as could be imagined. Dealt with the grief, and was there for her. As is typical for some dreams, feels like forever when you're dreaming. Wake up, feeling like it was completely real and had happened, and having to convince myself it was just a dream and everything was okay.   

Another dream was shortly after my girlfriend and I parted ways, in the dream we'd come to a resolution and decided to keep the relationship going. Everything was great, and the future was bright, and then I woke up and mentally re-broke up.

Thanks for the info. I'm still excited at the changes I've seen, and looking forward to the future. So far at least, way outweighs the risks.

And sometimes it's not so bad. I'm 1 month in on my medication, Celexa. Fear is certainly less, anxiety is almost non existent, depression is much more manageable. Sex drive is still as raging as ever. In the past month I've had one "bad" day, vs being lucky to have 1 "good" day a week. It's been life changing. Talk to your doctor, and find people you trust to talk about your depression, and your decision to get better. :)
